title: Underlying marked pairs, semistability and geometric stability
statement: For a scheme $T$, an underlying pair $P=(X,D,i)$ consists of two schemes over $T$ and a morphism $i:D\to X$ over $T$. Forgetting the property proofs of a multipointed curve [def-trf-multipointed-curve] gives such a pair. A pair is multipointed exactly when it is equal to the underlying pair of a multipointed curve in that sense; this retains flatness, finite presentation, pure relative dimensions $1$ and $0$ and the closed immersion, with empty marking permitted and no separatedness or properness assumption. The canonical base change of a pair along $g:T'\to T$ is $(X\times_TT',D\times_TT',i_{T'})$, using the pullback functor [def-pc-fibre-product]. The pair is semistable if it is multipointed, $D\to T$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], its image lies in the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and every nonsmooth point of each chosen algebraic-closure geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] is an ordinary double point, using the scalar-compatible maximal-ideal completion predicate of [def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data]. For an over-$T$ morphism $f:X\to Y$ of underlying pairs, geometric stability means that on every chosen geometric fibre there is no irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] isomorphic over its scalar field to the projective line [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], contracted by $f$ to a point and meeting the union of marking and nonsmooth locus in at most two distinct points. Such a component is represented by a closed immersion from the projective line whose range is an irreducible component; special points are counted in that range, not on its normalization.
